discovery: Metamaterials and metasurfaces: controlling light through subwavelength-structured artificial media
motivation: Pendry showed theoretically that artificial media built from subwavelength resonant elements can have electromagnetic properties absent in nature, including negative permeability, negative refraction and the perfect lens, and later founded transformation optics. Smith realized these ideas experimentally, demonstrating negative refraction (2000-2001) and the first electromagnetic cloak (2006). Capasso transformed the concept into flat optics: his generalized laws of reflection and refraction (2011) and ultrathin metasurface metalenses replaced bulky optical components with nanostructured planar layers. Together these contributions established a new paradigm in which light is controlled by design at the nanoscale rather than by the choice of material. The concepts are now used across physics, from super-resolution imaging and analog optical computing to wavefront shaping, sensing and photovoltaics, and metasurface optics has entered industrial manufacturing. This is a fundamental discovery with extraordinary reach from basic electromagnetism to technology.
